correctness.rationale: For any packet of radius r, each nonempty subset sum of the frame vectors joins vertices in a permutation simplex, hence has length ≤2r. In BCC, nonzero vectors of squared length <2 are exactly six axes and eight half diagonals; shell-compatible independent triples must be three same-parity half diagonals, exactly eight triples. Their six tetrahedra each have all four vertices at squared distance 5/16 from their centroid, and the mean-square identity proves this is the minimum fitting radius. Thus κ=√5/4 and these are the only frames below 1/√2. One explicit nonoptimal frame has a subset sum of length √2 and has six displayed fitting balls of squared radius at most 1/2. Exact rational checker.py confirms all 14 shell vectors, 232 independent shell triples, eight compatible triples, all 48 optimal packet simplices and the six witness balls.

value.rationale: The BCC lattice is a natural extremal Euclidean lattice-covering benchmark, and the new common-frame fitting invariant κ has only recently been introduced. An exact minimizing radius is useful, but the stronger result classifies every optimal independent frame (including potential nonbasis competitors) and proves an attained sharp positive next-level gap. This is a rigid discrete optimization statement not implied by knowing the classical BCC covering radius or one Delaunay tetrahedron.
